faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Common questions about HEIC to JPG conversion

items.question: What is HEIC format and why does Apple use it?
items.answer: HEIC (High Efficiency Image Container) is Apple's default photo format since iOS 11 (2017). It uses HEVC (H.265) compression, providing 40-50% better compression than JPG with same quality. Apple adopted HEIC to save iCloud storage and improve photo quality. However, HEIC has limited compatibility outside Apple ecosystem, making JPG conversion necessary for cross-platform sharing.

items.question: Will converting HEIC to JPG reduce image quality?
items.answer: Converting HEIC to JPG preserves visual quality when using high JPG quality settings (85-95). File size will increase 1.5-2x since JPG's compression is less efficient than HEVC. Use quality 85-90 for general use, 90-95 for important photos. The quality loss is minimal and imperceptible for most uses. Tradeoff is universal compatibility vs file size.

items.question: Why can't I open HEIC files on Windows or Android?
items.answer: HEIC requires HEVC (H.265) codec which isn't natively supported on Windows (requires codec pack) or Android. Apple uses HEIC for better compression but it's proprietary to Apple ecosystem. Converting to JPG ensures universal compatibility. JPG works on all devices without additional software. This is why HEIC to JPG conversion is essential for cross-platform photo sharing.

items.question: How do I convert iPhone photos to JPG automatically?
items.answer: iPhone Settings → Camera → Formats → Choose 'Most Compatible' to save photos as JPG instead of HEIC. For existing HEIC photos, use our converter to batch convert to JPG. Alternatively, enable 'Automatic' transfer setting which converts HEIC to JPG when sharing to non-Apple devices. For maximum compatibility, shoot in JPG mode or batch convert HEIC libraries.

items.question: Can I convert HEIC back to original quality?
items.answer: No, converting HEIC to JPG and back won't restore original quality. Each conversion between lossy formats causes cumulative quality loss. Always keep original HEIC files as backup if staying in Apple ecosystem. If you need to share photos, convert HEIC to JPG once at high quality (90-95) and keep both versions. Don't convert back and forth.

items.question: Is HEIC to JPG conversion free and secure?
items.answer: Yes, our HEIC to JPG converter is completely free with no registration, watermarks, or payment required. All conversion happens locally in your browser using WebAssembly - your photos never leave your device. This ensures 100% privacy and security, with no server uploads, data collection, or third-party access. HEIC decoding and JPG encoding are performed entirely client-side.
